title: The servant worth keeping
situation: A king has to choose whom to keep close, and the men who flatter him are the easiest to keep.
wise_response: The verse describes the servant worth keeping: one who arrives without being summoned, waits at the door, and answers with measured truth when asked.
why_it_worked: It rewards availability and restraint together. The flatterer is always available but never measured; the blunt man is measured but often absent.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keep the man who agrees with everything and is always in the room.
original_text:
yo 'nāhūtaḥ samabhyeti dvāri tiṣṭhati sarvadā |
pṛṣṭhaḥ satyaṃ mitaṃ brūte sa bhṛtyo 'rho mahībhujām ||
edition: Ramchandra Jha, 6th ed., Varanasi: Chowkhamba Vidyabhavan, 1991 (Vidyabhavana Sanskrit Grantha Mala 17); GRETIL sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra
ai_translation: He who comes without being called, who always stands at the door, and who, when asked, speaks the truth in measure — that servant is worthy of kings.

title: The king as gardener
situation: A ruler wants his realm to prosper and is deciding where the money should go.
wise_response: The verse compares him to a gardener: the people are the shoots, and giving and honour are the water. He is judged by whether they grow.
why_it_worked: It makes the ruler's own reward depend on the people's growth, so generosity becomes the mechanism of his interest rather than a virtue he can postpone.
tempting_wrong_answer: Keep the treasury full and call it prudence.
original_text:
phalārthī nṛpatir lokān pālayed yatnam āsthitaḥ |
dāna-mānādi-toyena mālākāro 'ṅkurān iva ||
edition: Ramchandra Jha, 6th ed., Varanasi: Chowkhamba Vidyabhavan, 1991 (Vidyabhavana Sanskrit Grantha Mala 17); GRETIL sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra
ai_translation: A king who seeks the fruit should protect his people with effort, watering them like a gardener waters shoots — with giving, honour, and the rest.

key_terms.phalārthin: one who seeks the fruit, the reward

title: The repair after harsh words
situation: A man has said something harsh in an argument and the room has gone quiet.
wise_response: The verse is the repair: it names the fault without excusing it — whether from ignorance or from knowing better — and asks forgiveness plainly.
why_it_worked: It asks without conditions and without a defence, which is what makes it possible for the other person to answer.
tempting_wrong_answer: Explain why the harsh words were justified, or wait for the other person to apologize first.
original_text:
ajñānāj jñānato vāpi duruktaṃ yad udāhṛtam |
mayā tat kṣamyatām adya dvābhyām api prasādataḥ ||
edition: Ramchandra Jha, 6th ed., Varanasi: Chowkhamba Vidyabhavan, 1991 (Vidyabhavana Sanskrit Grantha Mala 17); GRETIL sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra
ai_translation: Whatever harsh word was spoken by me, through ignorance or through knowledge, let it be forgiven today, by the grace of both.

title: No wealth like contentment
situation: A man has enough, and the people around him are acquiring more.
wise_response: The verse compares two kinds of possession: character as an ornament and contentment as wealth, and says nothing else is equal to either.
why_it_worked: It changes what counts as having. If contentment is wealth, then the race for more is not a way of getting richer.
tempting_wrong_answer: Measure himself against the people who have more, and call the difference a lack.
original_text:
vibhūṣaṇaṃ śīla-samaṃ na cānyat |
santoṣa-tulyaṃ dhanam asti nānyat ||
edition: Ramchandra Jha, 6th ed., Varanasi: Chowkhamba Vidyabhavan, 1991 (Vidyabhavana Sanskrit Grantha Mala 17); GRETIL sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra
ai_translation: There is no ornament equal to good character, and no wealth equal to contentment.
